assertions.title: ORD–LGA loading or failure states remain recoverable

steps.action: Open the supported loading probe URL.
steps.expected: ORD-LGA-specific loading messaging is visible with a recovery path.
steps.observed: The page showed 'ORD–LGA Price War Simulator', 'Recoverability probe active: route-level loading state remains visible before the live route is restored.', a 'Recovery path' section, and visible 'Open live route' plus 'Back to projects' actions.

steps.action: Open the supported error probe URL.
steps.expected: ORD-LGA-specific error messaging is visible with a recovery path.
steps.observed: The page showed 'Route Error', 'ORD–LGA Price War Simulator', 'Recoverability probe active: this route-level failure view keeps the recovery path explicit so validators can confirm the fallback stays user-visible under a controlled condition.', diagnostics mentioning '?routeProbe=error', and visible 'Open live route' plus 'Back to projects' actions.

steps.action: Check browser errors and observed requests after each probe flow.
steps.expected: No unexpected console errors and successful probe-route loading evidence are available.
steps.observed: No browser errors were captured in either probe flow. Network capture for the error probe showed GET /projects/ord-lga-price-war?routeProbe=error plus the expected Next.js static assets and follow-on fetches for live-route and navigation preloads.

evidence.network: Loading probe opened successfully on /projects/ord-lga-price-war?routeProbe=loading. Error probe network capture included GET /projects/ord-lga-price-war?routeProbe=error, the ORD-LGA page chunk, route error chunk, and follow-on RSC/navigation fetches; no failing requests were observed in the saved capture.
observedCopy: Recoverability probe active: route-level loading state remains visible before the live route is restored.
Recoverability probe active: this route-level failure view keeps the recovery path explicit so validators can confirm the fallback stays user-visible under a controlled condition.

frictions.description: On this Next.js App Router page, raw body-text capture included streamed payload/script text after the visible probe copy.
frictions.resolution: Used screenshots as the primary UI evidence and relied on the leading visible-copy portion of the saved text artifacts for exact messaging verification.

summary: Validated VAL-ORDLGA-006 on the shared production-like runtime using the two supported ORD-LGA routeProbe URLs. Both the loading and error probes displayed ORD-LGA-specific messaging and a visible recovery path, so the assertion passed.
